violated_contract: A chat composer's Send action must leave keyboard focus on the composer's own input afterward. A plain <button> click moves native DOM focus to the clicked button itself; if nothing explicitly reclaims it, typing the next message silently goes nowhere until the user clicks the input again. Enter-to-send never moves focus away, so the bug is mouse/trackpad-only and easy to miss in keyboard-driven testing. Relying on an unrelated focus effect (e.g. a view-change or remount effect keyed on navigation) to incidentally restore focus is not a guarantee: it only covers the specific transition that effect targets (e.g. the first send that flips an idle view into an active one), and does nothing for a same-view follow-up send, which is the common repeat-message case.
canonical_prevention: Every mouse-driven Send handler explicitly calls focus() on the composer's own input ref immediately after invoking the submit logic. The call is a harmless no-op on the Enter-to-send path, since focus never left the input there. A behavioral test drives Send via a real fireEvent.click (not keyDown) and asserts document.activeElement is the composer input afterward, so the regression can't hide behind keyboard-only coverage.
